:::{#cor-log-quot}
#### Logarithm of a quotient

If $a > 0$ and $b > 0$, then

$$\logf{\frac{a}{b}} = \logf{a} - \logf{b}$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: proof

Since $a > 0$ and $b > 0$, the quotient $\frac{a}{b}$ is positive,
so @thm-log-prod applies to the product $\frac{a}{b} \cd b$:

$$
\ba
\logf{a}
&= \logf{\frac{a}{b} \cd b}
&& \text{(} a = \tfrac{a}{b} \cd b \text{)}
\\
&= \logf{\frac{a}{b}} + \logf{b}
&& \text{(logarithm of a product)}
\ea
$$

The second step applies @thm-log-prod.
Subtracting $\logf{b}$ from both sides gives $\logf{a} - \logf{b} = \logf{\frac{a}{b}}$.

:::
